symbols.name: target length
symbols.meaning: The number of entries of the resampled vector, a power of two greater than $q$.
symbols.quote: Gaussian resampling replaces a [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) of arbitrary length $q$ by a transform of power-of-two length $W>q$.

symbols.name: Gaussian width
symbols.meaning: The width of the Gaussian weights, an integer at least 2 with $\sigma^2<p$.
symbols.quote: Let $\sigma$ be the width, an integer with $2\le\sigma$ and $\sigma^2<p$, where $p>100$ is the precision.

symbols.name: output index
symbols.meaning: The index of an entry of a length-$W$ output vector, running from $0$ to $W-1$.
symbols.quote: For a length-$q$ vector $u$ with entries $u_j$, $0\le j<q$ (indices read modulo $q$), and an output index $k$ with $0\le k<W$, let $\Psi$ and $\Xi$ be the Gaussian-weighted sums

symbols.name: first Gaussian map
symbols.meaning: The map sending a length-$q$ vector to a length-$W$ vector by Gaussian-weighted sums with weight $\exp(-\pi\sigma^{-2}(j-qk/W)^2)$.
symbols.quote: For a length-$q$ vector $u$ with entries $u_j$, $0\le j<q$ (indices read modulo $q$), and an output index $k$ with $0\le k<W$, let $\Psi$ and $\Xi$ be the Gaussian-weighted sums

symbols.name: second Gaussian map
symbols.meaning: The map sending a length-$q$ vector to a length-$W$ vector by Gaussian-weighted sums with weight $\exp(-\pi\sigma^{2}(Wj/q-k)^2)$.
symbols.quote: For a length-$q$ vector $u$ with entries $u_j$, $0\le j<q$ (indices read modulo $q$), and an output index $k$ with $0\le k<W$, let $\Psi$ and $\Xi$ be the Gaussian-weighted sums

symbols.name: selection map
symbols.meaning: The map that picks, for each $j<q$, the entry of a length-$W$ vector at the integer nearest $Wj/q$.
symbols.quote: Let $\mathcal J$ pick, for $0\le j<q$, entry $\lfloor Wj/q+\tfrac12\rfloor$ of a length-$W$ vector, the integer nearest $Wj/q$ with ties upward.

symbols.name: diagonal correction
symbols.meaning: The diagonal map multiplying entry $j$ by the factor that cancels the weight of $\Xi$ at position $j$.
symbols.quote: Let $\Upsilon$ multiply entry $j$ by $\exp\big(\pi\sigma^2(Wj/q-\lfloor Wj/q+\tfrac12\rfloor)^2\big)$, which cancels the weight of $\Xi$ at that position.

symbols.name: middle map
symbols.meaning: The length-$q$ map $\mathcal J\,\Xi\,\Upsilon$, which is close to the identity.
symbols.quote: Put $\mathcal N=\mathcal J\,\Xi\,\Upsilon$, a map from length $q$ to length $q$.

symbols.name: deviation from identity
symbols.meaning: The difference $I-\mathcal N$, whose norm is below one half.
symbols.quote: For $\mathcal X=I-\mathcal N$ with $\|\mathcal X\|<1/2$, the partial sums $\sum_{l=0}^{K}\mathcal X^l$ satisfy $(I-\mathcal X)\sum_{l=0}^{K}\mathcal X^l=I-\mathcal X^{K+1}\to I$, so $\mathcal N^{-1}=\sum_{l\ge0}\mathcal X^l$ and $\|\mathcal N^{-1}\|\le 2$.

symbols.name: first contraction
symbols.meaning: The map $\Psi/2$ from length $q$ to length $W$, which is a contraction.
symbols.quote: With $\mathcal E=\Psi/2$ and $\mathcal U=2^{1-2\sigma^2}\,\Upsilon\mathcal N^{-1}\mathcal J$, the constants multiply to $2^{2\sigma^2}\cdot2^{1-2\sigma^2}\cdot\tfrac12=1$, giving

symbols.name: second contraction
symbols.meaning: The map $2^{1-2\sigma^2}\,\Upsilon\mathcal N^{-1}\mathcal J$ from length $W$ to length $q$, which is a contraction.
symbols.quote: With $\mathcal E=\Psi/2$ and $\mathcal U=2^{1-2\sigma^2}\,\Upsilon\mathcal N^{-1}\mathcal J$, the constants multiply to $2^{2\sigma^2}\cdot2^{1-2\sigma^2}\cdot\tfrac12=1$, giving

symbols.name: length-q coordinate permutation
symbols.meaning: The permutation of length-$q$ vectors whose $j$-th entry is entry $Wj \bmod q$ of the input.
symbols.quote: Let $\Pi_q$ and $\Pi_W$ be the coordinate permutations $(\Pi_q u)_j=u_{Wj \bmod q}$ and $(\Pi_W u)_k=u_{-qk \bmod W}$, acting on vectors $u$ of length $q$ and $W$ respectively.

symbols.name: length-W coordinate permutation
symbols.meaning: The permutation of length-$W$ vectors whose $k$-th entry is entry $-qk \bmod W$ of the input.
symbols.quote: Let $\Pi_q$ and $\Pi_W$ be the coordinate permutations $(\Pi_q u)_j=u_{Wj \bmod q}$ and $(\Pi_W u)_k=u_{-qk \bmod W}$, acting on vectors $u$ of length $q$ and $W$ respectively.

relations.quote: Gaussian resampling replaces a [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) of arbitrary length $q$ by a transform of power-of-two length $W>q$.
It reshapes the transforms of the [radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md) that the integer product needs, so the later steps can use butterfly layers and polynomial transforms.
Gaussian resampling converts the lengths for the [synthetic polynomial transforms](synthetic-transforms.md) into powers of two.
Gaussian resampling replaces the Fourier transforms by [multidimensional transforms](multidimensional-transform.md) whose axis lengths are powers of two.
Gaussian resampling requires that $q$ and $W$ be [coprime](coprime.md), $\gcd(q,W)=1$, and $W/q-1>p/\sigma^4$.
Gaussian resampling measures contraction with the [array norm](array-norm.md).
